19 An electric motor operating a lift has an output power of 20 kW.
motor
cable
20 m
lift and
passengers
1500 kg
The lift and passengers have a combined mass of 1500 kg. The motor raises the lift through a
distance of 20 m.
How long does it take?
A
6 s
B
15 s
C
30 s
D
60 s

hints: Notice the motor output power is $20 \text{ kW} = 20000 \text{ W}$, the mass is $1500 \text{ kg}$ and the vertical height is $20 \text{ m}$.
Connect power to work and time with $P = W/t$, where the useful work here is the gain in gravitational potential energy $W = mgh$.
First calculate $mgh$ with $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, then rearrange to $t = mgh/P$ and check the result is near $15 \text{ s}$.
walkthrough: Identify the useful energy: raising the lift at steady speed increases gravitational potential energy by $\Delta E_p = mgh$.
State the power relation: output power is rate of useful work, so $P = W/t = mgh/t$.
Substitute values with units: $m = 1500 \text{ kg}$, $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, $h = 20 \text{ m}$, $P = 20 \text{ kW} = 20000 \text{ W}$.
Rearrange for time and evaluate: $t = W/P = 294300/20000 \approx 14.7 \text{ s}$, which rounds to $15 \text{ s}$ with sensible precision. This is option B.

A.explanation: Too short. It gives about $120000 \text{ J}$ of work, far less than the $mgh$ needed for $1500 \text{ kg}$ lifted $20 \text{ m}$.

B.explanation: The $mgh$ gain of about $300000 \text{ J}$ divided by $20000 \text{ W}$ gives about $15 \text{ s}$.

C.explanation: Too long by a factor of 2. It would correspond to only $10 \text{ kW}$ of useful power for this $mgh$ gain.

D.explanation: Too long by a factor of 4. It would correspond to only $5 \text{ kW}$ of useful power for this $mgh$ gain.
